facts.statement: The genus Deltoptychius was first described by Morris and Roberts in 1862.
Deltoptychius lived during the Carboniferous period in what is now the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: It lived in the Carboniferous period in present-day United Kingdom.

facts.statement: Fossils of Deltoptychius have been discovered in the Glencartholm Volcanic Beds Formation in Scotland.
facts.quote: Fossils of the genus have been found in the Glencartholm Volcanic Beds Formation of the Upper Border Group in Scotland.

facts.statement: Deltoptychius had large eyes adapted for hunting in deep waters and crushed shellfish using solid tooth plates.
facts.quote: Deltoptychius's large eyes allowed it to hunt in deep waters, crushing shellfish between solid tooth plates in its mouth.

facts.statement: Deltoptychius belongs to the family Deltoptychiidae.
Deltoptychius is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Deltoptychius lived between 346.7 and 298.9 million years ago, spanning the Visean to Gzhelian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Visean to Gzhelian (346.7 to 298.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Deltoptychius is Cochliodus acutus.

rejected.statement: Deltoptychius is an extinct cartilaginous fish related to modern chimaeras, named for its triangular and folded appearance.
rejected.quote: Deltoptychius (from Greek, 'triangle' and 'fold') is an extinct species of cartilaginous fish related to the modern chimaeras.

rejected.quote: Although it emerged over 300 million years ago, Deltoptychius was similar in appearance to modern-day chimaeras, possessing a long, whip-like tail and large, wing-like pectoral fins that it probably used to glide through the water.
